composition_parti.rule: The street (gable) elevation is deliberately off-axis -- two or three bays with the entrance bay off-centre or absent entirely, since the false door sits in the piazza screen wall, not in the house wall itself; the piazza flank alone carries a regular five-bay rhythm.
composition_parti.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'strict-bilateral-symmetry... forbidding a picturesque or balanced-asymmetrical parti outright' from georgian-colonial-american -- directly contradicted by this node's own proportional_system.bay_rhythm: 'entrance bay off-centre or absent entirely (the false door sits in the piazza screen).' Georgian bilateral symmetry is real on the five-bay piazza flank (window_grouping_rule, below) but not on the street gable, and the family-of-origin binding could not make that distinction.

variants.note: defining_characteristics[0]: 'One room wide, turned so the narrow gable end faces the street; two or three bays to the street, five to the flank'. diagnostic_tells[1]: 'The street elevation is a gable end two or three bays wide, with the long piazza visible in perspective down the lot'. The ridge runs the long axis; its gable end is what the street sees.

Demoted from canonical. The record's defining characteristic and its tells give the street a gable end, which a hipped roof lacks; exemplars[4] records one hipped example, 'a hipped roof and a two-storey wrought-iron balcony on the street front', and that example is the node's `standing: icon`, whose why reads 'The HABS form calls it the 'earliest existing example of Charleston "single house"''. So the hip is admitted, not the default, on defining_characteristics[0]'s word against the icon's own roof. Judgment.

roof_form.rule: A side-gable roof whose narrow gable end is turned to the street (defining_characteristics[0]); the composed elevation is the piazza flank.
roof_form.note: BOUND 1 Oct 2026 (WP-16.9), on Lucas's answer B1 of 30 Sep 2026, recorded in oq/the-roof-is-drawn-side-gabled-whatever-the-style-says: charleston-single-house binds its own roof_form. Until then it wrote none and resolved GEORGIAN-COLONIAL-AMERICAN's record through charleston-georgian: `side-gable` and `hip` canonical, neither carrying a note. The side gable is this record's own: defining_characteristics[0] 'One room wide, turned so the narrow gable end faces the street; two or three bays to the street, five to the flank' and diagnostic_tells[1] 'The street elevation is a gable end two or three bays wide, with the long piazza visible in perspective down the lot'. A hip has no gable end to turn to the street, so it is not this type's default. It stays permitted, and the demotion is a reading: the building the type's origin is argued from is hipped -- exemplars[4], the Robert Brewton House, `standing: icon`, 'a hipped roof and a two-storey wrought-iron balcony on the street front', which its why calls the HABS form's 'earliest existing example of Charleston "single house"'. The demotion moves no drawing: the roof layer keeps side-gable where it is canonical. Marked judgment for the hip's demotion and the front gable's reading. Under a specified binding (T5, taken as recommended under Lucas's standing instruction of 1 Oct 2026 and never put to him) georgian-colonial-american's slot rule and its three parameters stop at this record: hip_ridge_length_ratio (editorial, 0.25 to 0.5), and gambrel_lower_pitch and gambrel_upper_pitch (measured, 20:12 and 9:12, for New England and the Hudson Valley). They are not copied: each copied measured figure would be a new unsourced measured parameter in this kit, which check_kits.py refuses by identity (build/measured_unsourced_grandfathered.json names them for georgian-colonial-american alone). An extends delta over the writer's record would keep them.

chimney.rule: Chimneys sit on the rear wall or the blind flank, never symmetrically paired on the street gable (own diagnostic tell).
chimney.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Georgian gable-end-paired chimney rule directly contradicted by this node's own diagnostic_tells: 'Chimneys on the rear wall or the blind flank rather than symmetrically paired on the street gable.'

window_grouping_rule.rule: The street gable carries two or three bays with the entrance bay off-centre or absent; the piazza flank carries five even bays with the true entrance in the second bay from the street, column spacing 8 to 10 ft.
window_grouping_rule.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'single-openings-odd-bays... entrance in the centre bay' from georgian-colonial-american -- true of the piazza flank but false of the street gable, which is this type's own most distinctive composition and the opposite of a centred entrance.

variants.note: Charleston's narrow, deep lots are historically served by a rear service lane; a small detached garage there continues the same footprint the detached kitchen dependency already occupies.
A garage door on the street gable would occupy the same narrow frontage the false door and piazza screen depend on, destroying the type's single most recognisable move.

garage_strategy.rule: The car is housed in a small structure at the rear of the deep lot, reached from the service lane where one exists, in the footprint tradition already occupied by the detached kitchen dependency.
garage_strategy.note: No historical precedent exists for this slot. Authored per docs/inheritance.md's guidance -- this node's own text states the type 'has never actually stopped being built' on the Charleston peninsula, making it one of the clearest contemporary-buildable cases in this batch.

hearth_position.rule: Hearths sit at the rear wall or the blind flank, following the chimney position (chimney, above) -- not paired symmetrically about the passage axis at the gable ends, which is the inherited Georgian answer for a house seen frontally.
hearth_position.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Georgian gable-end-paired hearth rule that presupposes the house is composed frontally -- own street_relationship (already correctly resolving from charleston-georgian) states directly that 'the house is not seen frontally as the inherited Georgian family assumes.'

room_adjacency_overrides.rule: The street door opens onto the PIAZZA, not into the house. There is no entrance hall to reach, and the piazza is the entrance sequence.

rules.statement: The street door opens onto the PIAZZA, not into the house. There is no entrance hall to reach, and the piazza is the entrance sequence.
rules.why: rooms/piazza.json states it as the type's defining move -- 'entered from the street through a door in a screen that is not the house's door' -- and rooms/entry-porch.json's universal rule requires an entrance hall through a direct door. A single house has neither the hall nor the door the rule assumes. This is the first suppression declared in the corpus; the mechanism was built under OQ 15 and had nothing to carry until OQ 43 made the rule fire.

rules.statement: The piazza is the entrance sequence at BOTH levels. The upper piazza is reached from the stair and serves the chambers off it; there is no upper entrance hall and there is none below either.
rules.why: The suppression already declared on this node covers the street door (entry-porch). The upper piazza fails the same universal assumption through rooms/piazza.json's own rule, and for the same reason: this type's entrance sequence is a covered outdoor room, not a hall.

flank_setback_ft.note: Own hard constraint c05: at or within 3 ft of the property line.

setback_rule.rule: The flank opposite the piazza sits at or within 3 ft of the property line and carries no more than token openings -- a fire wall, a response to the Charleston fires of 1740 and 1778 (own hard constraint c05).
setback_rule.note: Restates own c05 directly; this slot was previously unresolved (open) despite the node's own text speaking to it directly.

landscape_idiom.rule: The walled garden, the piazza, and the detached kitchen dependency together form one privacy and climate system, regulating sightlines from the street as much as composing a formal geometric garden.
landscape_idiom.note: CASCADE FIX (partial -- a real garden exists, but its logic is privacy/climate, not purely axial composition). Before this binding, the slot resolved a generic Georgian 'geometric-forecourt' idiom; grounded instead in own long description: 'the walled garden, the detached dependency and the gated piazza are a system for regulating who can see whom.'
